title: A visible drain
bodyMd:
A fictional park replaced a buried pipe with a shallow planted channel carrying rainwater toward a retention basin. The landscape team described the channel as both infrastructure and a way for visitors to notice water moving through the site. During dry weather it often contained no visible water. Some visitors therefore assumed that it was broken.

The team added signs explaining that intermittent flow was expected and showing how the channel worked during storms. It also retained inspection procedures, since an empty channel after rain could indicate a blockage upstream. Visibility made part of the system understandable, but did not make its operation self-explanatory. The designers learned that exposing infrastructure can invite public attention while still requiring interpretation and maintenance.
